discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including giant TMR in crystalline MgO barriers

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently demonstrated large, reproducible tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions. This turned Julliere's low-temperature curiosity into a robust quantum-transport phenomenon: spin-dependent tunnelling set by the interfacial electronic structure. Parkin's 2004 work on sputtered crystalline MgO barriers, which realised the symmetry-filtering mechanism predicted by theory, raised TMR to hundreds of percent. That made magnetic tunnel junctions the central element of modern spintronics. The consequences have been confirmed in countless laboratories and in industry. MTJs have been the read sensor in every hard-disk drive for two decades, and they are the storage element of commercial spin-transfer-torque MRAM. They also serve as the essential platform for experiments on spin-transfer and spin-orbit torques. This discovery joins fundamental spin-polarised quantum tunnelling to device physics of global technological importance, and it complements the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
